about: Inputs for bellycapacity.html. Aircraft limits and standard masses come from the public sources named in 'sources'; everything else is an illustrative assumption, not any airline's data.

aircraft.name: Boeing 787-9
aircraft.source: Boeing, 787 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, D6-58333 Rev P (December 2024), section 2.1.2, page 2-3: maximum design takeoff, landing and zero fuel weights, usable fuel, lower deck volume (20 + 16 LD-3 containers of 4.5 m3 and 11.4 m3 bulk), 290 seats in the dual-class layout.

dowNote: Dry operating weight (empty aircraft with crew, catering and water). Not in the Boeing document; illustrative.
massSource: EASA AMC1 CAT.POL.MAB.100(e), Annex to ED Decision 2012/018/R: standard mass 84 kg per adult passenger including hand baggage, 15 kg per checked bag on intercontinental flights.

route.note: Illustrative: a 9,800 km sector flown westbound, into the prevailing westerlies, at a true airspeed of 900 km/h, plus 0.4 hours for taxi, climb and descent.

fuel.note: Illustrative: each hour of flight burns 2.5% of the aircraft's weight (Breguet range equation); 7,000 kg kept for the alternate airport and final reserve, plus 5% of the trip fuel for contingency.

wind.note: Illustrative: average headwind component on the route, in km/h, from 100 in late January to 15 in late July, day-to-day spread 30 km/h with weather spells that last a few days. 'skill' is the share of the day-to-day spread a forecast made that many days ahead explains.

pax.note: Illustrative: the airline accepts up to 300 bookings for 290 seats; 96% turn up. Average demand ranges from 260 bookings in the quiet season to 300 at the July peak, 12% spread from one departure to the next. Half the bookings are made by 35 days out.

bags.note: Illustrative: 1.05 checked bags per passenger in winter to 1.25 in summer, 0.08 spread from flight to flight, known only at check-in. The first 70 bags go in the bulk hold, the rest 40 to an LD-3.

cargo.note: Illustrative: freight fills 80% of a container's volume; cargo on the route averages 165 kg per m3; US$2.60 per kg flown and US$4.00 per kg offloaded (the cargorm.html defaults). Booked cargo turns up at 82% of its booked weight on average, 7 points spread from flight to flight. Requests total 1.6 times the average capacity, half of them in the last 5 days.
